DCML_DLC.unit: score-time event with analyst-coded cadence in 1283 annotated compositions across DLC; three subcorpora used in first pilot
DCML_DLC.local_evidence: Chopin Mazurkas, Mozart Piano Sonatas and Bach English/French Suites notes and harmonies TSV checked out at pinned upstream SHAs; movement siblings grouped by K or BWV identifier
DCML_DLC.limits: Analyst-annotated cadences are musicological structural judgments, NOT human emotions, tension curves, or independent ratings; the benchmark uses no expert key or chord as features. Scores are symbolic not performance MIDI. Licensed CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

CUDDY_LUNNEY_1995.unit: eight two-note melodic contexts, each followed by 25 probe pitches; published mean ratings from 12 trained and 12 untrained listeners
CUDDY_LUNNEY_1995.local_evidence: 1995 paper publishes 8 x 25 x 2 group means; 2025 thesis GitHub commit e9eb23384393c83de97e1a69d00133ae4673c425 supplies digitized cudlun95.data and eight context+placeholder MIDI files
CUDDY_LUNNEY_1995.limits: 400 group-mean cells are NOT 400 independent human participants; no raw listener responses, no audio timbre, no emotion tags. Reconstructed MIDI all anchor on F#4 whereas the primary study includes C4 and F#4 contexts, so interpretation is transposition-relative and exploratory.

SCHELLENBERG_1996.unit: eight real British folk melody fragments, fifteen diatonic probes each, published mean goodness-of-continuation from twenty different listeners
SCHELLENBERG_1996.local_evidence: Schellenberg (1996) Experiment 1 Appendix A published 120 means; 2025 thesis GitHub commit e9eb23384393c83de97e1a69d00133ae4673c425 supplies schell96.data, eight reconstructed MIDI/Kern fragments and documented descending-probe reversal
SCHELLENBERG_1996.limits: Independent listeners from Cuddy but eight fragment means only; not individual votes, not emotional labels. The source uses long melodies and 15 within-key diatonic probes rather than Cuddy's two-note contexts and 25 chromatic probes; an added final MIDI note is an artificial placeholder.

MANZARA_WITTEN_1992.unit: per-actual-note information-content bits derived from human anticipation bets on two Bach chorale melodies, 29 and 57 notes
MANZARA_WITTEN_1992.local_evidence: 1992 Waikato primary human gambling study and 2025 thesis commit e9eb23384393c83de97e1a69d00133ae4673c425, manzetal92.data 29+57 note rows (average/weighted/best aggregation) with corresponding chorale151.mid and chorale61.mid checked, 86 note-on events
MANZARA_WITTEN_1992.limits: Information content of the actually realized next note inferred from 15 listeners on chorale 151 and six selected listeners on chorale 61; NOT 86 independent subjects, NOT 25-way continuation goodness or musical emotion. Only two parent works, strong dependence between note rows, possible selection effects in second round; raw individual bets unavailable.

partitura_tension.limit: Tonal proxies, not a measured emotion or original instrument timbre.

music21_harmony.limit: An inferred chord/function is not an annotated ground truth or human feeling.

melody_features.limit: Published feature extraction is not validated human continuation prediction.

jsymbolic.limit: Global/windowed MIDI descriptors, not original acoustic spectrum, envelope or timbre.

idyom_original.limit: Import/launcher exist, but no original Lisp execution is reported in AnaMu.

idyom_thesis_precomputed.limit: The 2025 thesis provides probabilities previously computed by IDyOM; AnaMu did not run it. The original .dat, corpus provenance and test overlap remain unverified; this is not an interchangeable executable predictor or an emotion label.

cadential_note_context_proxy.limit: AnaMu exploratory note-only classifier, not DCML's analytic annotations, an original published cadence detector, or affect prediction.

cuddy_narmour_proxy.limit: Fixed feature approximation inspired by original interval expectancy and tonal hierarchy results, not the original Narmour or Schellenberg formula; grouped context-CV on published means is an exploratory reanalysis, not emotion recognition.
